source_checks.finding: FTC consumer alert (2020). The second paragraph supports the excerpt verbatim: "The scammers may say they have access to your computer or webcam", followed by "That's all talk." The card's section name "What the scammers claim" is not a heading on the page; the content sits in the second paragraph. The alert does not mention a screenshot, a Friday deadline, or replying to ask for proof. The warning applies to any phone or computer, as the card says.

Same FTC page. Verbatim support: "They threaten to distribute the video to your friends and family within hours", and the page also says the emails claim they "hacked into your computer and recorded you visiting adult websites." Applies to any phone or computer.

Same FTC page. Verbatim support: "Stop. Don't pay anything. Delete the message. It's a scam." The card's section name "Advice, opening steps" is not a heading; the sentence is in the first paragraph. Applies to any phone or computer.
Same FTC page. Verbatim support: "please report it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov". The card's section name "Reporting" is not a heading on the page. Applies to any phone or computer.

required_actions.action: Do not pay the scammer anything
Know that the claim of webcam or computer access is talk, not proof of a real threat
Report the message to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
